PDF to CSV

Reads a folder of PDFs, pulls mapped fields into CSV. Works offline: this page cannot make network requests.

Template

Type the field names in Fields by name: that is all a run needs. A sample PDF is optional: open one to see what each field reads before running a whole folder, to have the labels detected, or to drag a box around a value that has no label. Comparing a few more records of the same form makes the detection surer. The template holds field names, labels, box positions and the sample's drawn lines only, never record content.

no sample loaded

Fields by name

One field per line, written the way its label appears on the form. Case, spacing and punctuation do not matter. Alternate spellings: Work Item No | WI Number. Required: end the line with *. A label that appears in several blocks: Approved By > Date reads the Date inside the Approved By block; Date #3 reads the third Date on the form. Each label is looked for on every page of the form, and the value is read beside it or just below it.

Log

Download

  • records.csv: one row per record that held the main form. Opens in Excel (UTF-8, Japanese safe).
  • problems.csv: every file that could not be read, had no text layer, lacked the main form, or is missing required fields, with the reason.
  • needs-ocr.txt: paths of files with no text layer. Run these through Acrobat Pro (Scan & OCR, Recognize Text, batch) and read them again.
  • record-text.jsonl: optional, one line per record with the main form's text only, for a retrieval index.
  • record-chunks.jsonl: optional, the same records cut for a retrieval index at three zoom levels: the whole record, one line per field, and paragraph-sized chunks of long fields. Each line names its file, form, field and pages, and points to the level above it.
